gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Carpuride's own WF01 wireless rear camera cannot be used with the W903, ChatGPT's top pick. The W903 instead takes a wired rear camera chosen by device version. The front-camera-only W903 caps its microSD (TF) card at 64 GB, while the W903S takes up to 128 GB, and every W903 listing excludes HarmonyOS and Huawei P and Mate phones.
standout_why: I opened the Motorys guide (2026-05-27), which lists the Carpuride W903 but gives no Android version, no Huawei or HarmonyOS exclusion, no card limit, no rear-camera accessory compatibility and only 12 V power. I also opened the JADO guide, which gives only general rules (iPhone 6s or newer on iOS 9+ for wireless CarPlay, Android 11+ for wireless Android Auto) and no card or rear-accessory limits for any model. The cited Road & Track page and Car and Driver were blocked to my fetcher. DashGear Lab and ScoutVetted failed with certificate errors, and RottenWifi timed out. So I could not check those five pages, and the standout score rests on Motorys and JADO.
decides: This keeps the W903 as the pick but changes which version to buy. A shopper who wants rear recording should buy the $249.99 dual-camera W903 bundle, not the $219.99 front-only one. Adding Carpuride's wireless WF01 later is not an option, because the maker excludes the W903. A shopper who wants more than 64 GB of storage, or a cabin camera, should look at the W903S ($279.90, up to 128 GB). Huawei and HarmonyOS phone owners should skip every Carpuride W903 version. For the Rexing alternative, the maker's spare FM charger works with the CPDuo-686, CPDuo-6.25, CPDuo-7, CPDuo Pro and CPStream, so it can replace a lost charger in a 12 V or 24 V vehicle. The CPDuo-9 mounts fit no other Rexing model.
